title: AdaptiveObserverCache: persistent observer state changes how frozen memory is read
summary: AdaptiveObserverCache now reaches a real two-timescale Qwen system. The earlier gates established that persistent observer state can change frozen-memory retrieval, while Gate 3 exposed slot/order confounding and Gates 4–7 rebuilt durable provenance/current-address binding. The Qwen branch then found a second boundary: geometry-steerable heads need not be downstream-causal. Causally selected frozen heads produced a real valve/sensor language switch, but held-out transfer passed the graded likelihood direction on 4/4 conflicts while only 2/4 generated answers fully switched. An order-only attacker isolated a very large first-record prior yet found nearly identical A-relative observer slopes under AB and BA order (7.91 versus 8.18), so the frozen effect is not merely a slot coordinate. The live harness now keeps one DynamicCache growing across turns and a separate evidence-derived observer state outside the prompt; the first successful second turn grew 131→160 tokens with old source rows fixed and byte-stable while an external B receipt changed m to -0.664. Attention moved strongly toward B, but generation stayed on A, leaving temporal-distance versus control-strength as the next clean discriminator.

nodes.claim: Tests whether a frozen transformer can carry a persistent observer/evidence state outside the prompt and a genuinely growing KV cache, so external receipts alter how unchanged historical sources are read later without rewriting model weights or old source K/V.
nodes.survived: DistilGPT2 Gates 2–7 establish persistent retrieval control, expose and then factor slot/order from provenance identity, and infer current identity from history. On Qwen3-8B, causally selected frozen heads produced a natural-language valve/sensor switch. Held-out transfer then moved complete A-vs-B sequence likelihood in the intended direction on 4/4 unrelated conflicts, with 2/4 full generation switches and 2/2 reversed-order switches. The order-only attacker found nearly identical observer slopes under AB and BA physical order (7.9095 vs 8.1761; ratio 1.034) despite the unmodified model's ±10.8 first-record prior. The live cache harness then completed a real second turn: cache/history grew 131→160 tokens, original source spans remained A=[45,62), B=[72,87), cache integrity stayed true, and external B evidence changed anchored trust to -0.664 while selected-head target mass became 0.2532 vs 0.0362 for A.
nodes.killed: Several stronger stories failed. Geometry steering alone did not reliably change Qwen language; causal head selection was required. The frozen Qwen plan did not meet the preregistered strong-transfer gate (2/4 held-out generation switches, not >=3/4), so the current result is a graded directional control rather than a guaranteed binary switch. The first order-attacker verdict code also overstated the result because BA likelihood crossed at m=+1 while greedy generation did not; the code now reports that case as likelihood-only identity behavior. In the first successful live second turn, m=-0.664 moved attention strongly toward B but the answer remained valve/A, so robust language-level control across increasing cache distance is not established.

edges.why: AinsteinInside's Gate 0.7d made the measuring apparatus itself a live variable when harmless execution geometry changed tiny causal conclusions. AdaptiveObserverCache turns that methodological lesson into a mechanism: observer state is explicit and changes how frozen transformer memory is read.

OperatorTime established the abstract form that resident history can change the effective operator available now even when parameters stay fixed. AdaptiveObserverCache instantiates that idea as a persistent reader state that changes the effective attention/query operator over unchanged memory.

ReadWrite shows that what is knowable depends on the probe/intervention rather than on passive state alone. AdaptiveObserverCache moves that bounded-observer idea inside transformer memory: the current query geometry determines which distinction in frozen K/V becomes visible.

WhatToLookAt makes remembered relations change which later measurement is worth buying. AdaptiveObserverCache Gate 7 reaches the same boundary from transformer memory: history constrains current identity, and the next planned gate explicitly prices which probe the observer should purchase.

PredictiveHKT warns that changing representation coordinates can impersonate world/operator change. AdaptiveObserverCache's identity/alias gates separate durable provenance from its current surface key/address, making coordinate translation an explicit part of memory reuse.

AuditedEpistemicCache records provenance and representation-generation receipts so old evidence is not blindly reused. AdaptiveObserverCache turns that bookkeeping principle into a read operation: old trust/history is rebound to the current representation before it may control retrieval.

AInstein's provenance-misbinding controls show that having the right ingredients with the wrong addresses can yield confident failure. AdaptiveObserverCache makes source identity/address binding a first-class operation before attention is steered.
